names.note: Read out of doxologia.ro's line for 25 noiembrie, «Sfânta Mare Muceniță Ecaterina», with the rank words left off.

Read out of the Охридски пролог's heading for 24. новембар ст. ст., „Св. вел. мученица Екатерина.“ — «Св.» is “saint” and not a rank and «вел. мученица» is the `great-martyr` grade `types` already keeps, so both come off and the heading prints nothing else; Alexandria is in the body. Measured: no other folder in the corpus holds this string and it joins no fold.

birth.note: saint.gr heads the page «Αγια Αικατερινη (282 - 304)». The year is that page's and the corpus has had none before; days.pravoslavie.ru, which the folder's death interval comes from, gives no year of birth.

death.note: The two sources disagree and the interval records the disagreement. saint.gr: «μαρτύρησε στις αρχές του 4ου αιώνα μ.Χ. (304 μ.Χ.)», and it heads the page «(282 - 304)». days.pravoslavie.ru prints the reign «305-313» rather than a year, which is where the folder's earlier interval came from. Neither has been preferred here.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 24 ноября ст. ст. — «Вмц. Екатерины (305-313)»
Calendarul zilei, Doxologia (doxologia.ro), 25 noiembrie — «Sfânta Mare Muceniță Ecaterina»
saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 25ης Νοεμβρίου — «Αγία Αικατερίνη»

attestations.note: The life page `https://www.saint.gr/1060/saint.aspx` heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 25 Νοεμβρίου εκάστου έτους» and «Αγια Αικατερινη (282 - 304)», the same day the folder's Romanian row already carries, and the woman is the folder's own: the noblewoman of Alexandria who silenced the rhetors and was beheaded. **The page's years do not agree with the folder's existing death interval**, which comes from days.pravoslavie.ru's reign «305-313»: saint.gr heads her 282 to 304 and says «μαρτύρησε στις αρχές του 4ου αιώνα μ.Χ. (304 μ.Χ.)». The disagreement is recorded as a widened interval with both sources quoted in the note, which is what `docs/CORPUS.md` §3 asks for, and the reader's report names it as a thing an author may want to rule on. No `names` row is added: the folder already stores the Greek form «Αἰκατερίνη». The hymns taken are the page's Έτερον Ἀπολυτίκιον (Κατέβασμα) and its first Κοντάκιον, both of which name her and no other saint and both of which carry an ἦχος and a model; its first Ἀπολυτίκιον, «Ἡ ἀμνάς σου Ἰησοῦ», is the common of a woman martyr, names nobody and has no model, the Κάθισμα is neither a troparion nor a kontakion, and the page's «Έτερον Κοντάκιον» was not read, so none of the three is drafted. The page adds relics incorrupt at Sinai, a finger in the Buckingham Palace collection in London, and portions at Chilandari on Athos, at a church of her name in Nea Liosia in Attica, at Kykkos in Cyprus and at the Lavra of Saint Alexander Nevsky in Saint Petersburg. No asterisk and not the sentence «Δεν είναι διασταυρωμένη η ύπαρξη του Αγίου».

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 07.12.2025 (24. новембар ст. ст.) — „Св. вел. мученица Екатерина.“

attestations.note: The day's first entry, and the row's own note said pravoslavno.rs had not been read for this saint at all. `dates` UNTOUCHED: the book beheads her «24. новембра 310. године», and 310 is INSIDE the «304–313» this folder already holds as the disagreement between saint.gr's 304 and the Russian calendar's reign 305–313, so nothing is narrowed and nothing widened. A SMALL INCONSISTENCY RECORDED AND NOT RESOLVED: the same sentence puts her death «у својој 18. години», in her eighteenth year, which with the 282 birth this folder holds from saint.gr would give about 300 and not 310 — two of the three figures are this book's and the third is another's, and no reader may pick among them. No `related` row added: the empress Augusta-Basilissa, the stratelates Porphyrius with his two hundred soldiers and the company of philosophers are all three already related both ways. A COUNT THAT DISAGREES, recorded: this book says FIFTY wise men were called to dispute with her and fifty were burned, where the folder's companion is `hundred-and-fifty-rhetors`, a hundred and fifty; no folder was touched and neither number was changed. WHAT THE ENTRY ADDS: her father the emperor Costus and her life at Alexandria with her mother after his death; the mother a secret Christian who brought her to the faith through her own spiritual father; THE RING RECEIVED FROM THE LORD JESUS IN A VISION AS A TOKEN OF BETROTHAL, WHICH THE BOOK SAYS IS ON HER HAND TO THIS DAY; her learning in Greek philosophy, medicine, rhetoric and logic and her unusual bodily beauty; the confession of Christ by the philosophers before their burning; the angel who stopped and broke the wheel; the Lord himself appearing afterwards to comfort her; MILK FLOWING FROM HER BODY INSTEAD OF BLOOD; and her wonderworking relics resting on Sinai. Measured: no other folder holds «Екатерина».

hymns.text: Cu înțelepciunea ca și cu razele soarelui ai luminat pe filosofii păgâni și ca o lună prealuminoasă, care strălucea în noaptea necredinței, întunericul l-ai gonit; iar pe împărăteasa o ai încredințat, dimpreună și pe prigonitorul l-ai mustrat, de Dumnezeu chemată, fericită Ecaterino!Cu bucurie ai alergat la cămara cea cerească, către Hristos, Mirele cel preafrumos, și de la Dânsul te-ai încununat cu cunună împărătească, înaintea Căruia împreună cu îngerii stând, roagă-te pentru noi, cei ce cinstim sfântă pomenirea ta.

source.text: Doxologia — Troparul Sfintei Mari Mucenițe Ecaterina

english.text: With wisdom, as with the rays of the sun, you enlightened the pagan philosophers; and like a most radiant moon shining in the night of unbelief you drove the darkness away. You brought the empress to faith and rebuked the persecutor as well, Catherine called of God and blessed. With joy you ran to the heavenly bridal chamber, to Christ the most beautiful Bridegroom, and from him you were crowned with a royal crown; standing before him with the angels, pray for us who honour your holy memory.

hymns.text: Τὴν πανεύφημον νύμφην Χριστοῦ ὑμνήσωμεν, Αἰκατερίναν τὴν θείαν καὶ πολιοῦχον Σινᾶ, τὴν βοήθειαν ἡμῶν καὶ ἀντίληψιν· ὅτι ἐφίμωσε λαμπρῶς, τοὺς κομψοὺς τῶν ἀσεβῶν, τοῦ Πνεύματος τῇ δυνάμει, καὶ νῦν ὡς Μάρτυς στεφθεῖσα, αἰτεῖται πᾶσι τὸ μέγα ἔλεος.

source.text: saint.gr, Έτερον Ἀπολυτίκιον (Κατέβασμα), Ἦχος πλ. α’, Τὸν συνάναρχον Λόγον — on the page of «Αγία Αικατερίνη». It names her and no other saint. The page's first apolytikion is the common of a woman martyr and names nobody.

english.text: Let us sing of the all-praised bride of Christ, the divine Catherine, patroness of Sinai, our help and our support; for she splendidly silenced the clever men of the impious by the power of the Spirit, and now, crowned as a martyr, she asks great mercy for all.

hymns.text: Τὴν σοφίαν ἄνωθεν, κομισαμένη τοῦ λόγου, τῶν ῥητόρων ἤλεγξας, τὰς φληναφίας εὐτόνως· κάλλεσι, τῆς παρθενίας ὡραϊσμένη, αἵμασι, τῆς μαρτυρίας πεποικιλμένη· διὰ τοῦτό σε ὡς νύμφην, Αἰκατερίνα Χριστὸς προσήκατο.

source.text: saint.gr, Κοντάκιον, Ἦχος γ’, Ἡ Παρθένος σήμερον — on the page of «Αγία Αικατερίνη». It names her and no other saint. The page prints a second kontakion in Ἦχος β’, Τὰ ἄνω ζητῶν, whose text was not read and which is therefore not drafted.

english.text: Having received the wisdom of the word from above, you refuted the rhetors' idle talk with vigour; adorned with the beauties of virginity and embroidered with the blood of martyrdom. For this Christ received you, Catherine, as his bride.

hymns.text: Добродетельми, яко лучами солнечными,/ просветила еси неверныя мудрецы,/ и, якоже пресветлая луна ходящим в нощи,/ неверия тьму отгнала еси/ и царицу уверила еси,/ вкупе же и мучителя обличила еси,/ богозванная невесто, блаженная Екатерино,/ желанием востекла еси в Небесный чертог/ к прекрасному Жениху Христу,/ и от Него царским венцем венчалася еси:/ Емуже, со Ангелы предстоящи,/ за ны молися,// творящия пречестную память твою.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 24 ноября ст. ст. — «Тропарь великомученицы Екатерины»

english.text: With thy virtues, as with the rays of the sun, thou didst enlighten the unbelieving philosophers; and like the bright moon to those who walk by night thou didst drive off the darkness of unbelief, didst bring the empress to faith and at the same time didst rebuke the persecutor, O bride called of God, blessed Catherine. With longing thou didst run up to the heavenly bridal chamber, to the most beautiful Bridegroom Christ, and from him wast crowned with a royal crown. Standing before him with the angels, pray for us who keep thy most honourable memory.

hymns.text: Лик честный Божественне, мучениколюбцы,/ воздвигните ныне,/ почитающе всемудрую Екатерину,/ сия бо в тризнищи Христа проповеда и змия попра,// риторов разумы укротивши.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 24 ноября ст. ст. — «Кондак великомученицы Екатерины»

english.text: Raise up now an honourable choir in godly fashion, O lovers of the martyrs, honouring the all-wise Catherine; for in the arena she preached Christ and trampled the serpent, having tamed the minds of the rhetors.

hymns.text: Витийствующи днесь, Екатерина мученица/ и витиям обличи умовредную ересь,/ Ангел бо с Небесе к той прийде, силу от Вышняго принесе,/ юже приемши, мужески рече:/ Христос есть мучеником похвала.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 24 ноября ст. ст. — «Ин кондак великомученицы Екатерины»

english.text: Speaking today as an orator, the martyr Catherine rebuked the orators for their mind-harming error; for an angel came to her from heaven and brought her strength from the Most High, and receiving it she said manfully: Christ is the boast of the martyrs.
